a.text: It's one thing to make me play Go with you because you're bored, dear brother, it's another to use the pieces to form the character for 'bored.'
I can see you haven't practiced the Go theory I taught you.
As if that would help me against you.
It's true that the character on the board doesn't look as nice as your handwriting.
Why don't you find something else to pass the time, if it's not really a Go game that you're after? Go hiking, learn an instrument... I could teach you calligraphy, if it comes down to that.
The Go match may have been devoid of interest, but there's meaning in reading my opponent's thoughts from the movement of the pieces.
Oh? What thoughts did you read this time?

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: Hey, lou sai, what gives? This show skipped from episode seventeen to episode twenty!

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Happens with a scratched disc. Must've been the sand. Just deal with it, it's not that bad.

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: It was a key moment! Qi Qingqiu and Shen Feibai were at each other's throats a moment before, then suddenly they're fighting side-by-side? How'd we get there?

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: Qi Qingqiu finds out Shen Feibai killed his shifu, and sets out to kill him in turn.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: When he arrives at Yumen, however, he finds Shen Feibai a high-ranking officer in the military.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: With invaders at the gates, Qi Qingqiu suffers a sleepless night and realizes that there is more at stake than personal vengeance, so he joins the Grandmaster's banner to face the foe.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: It's a simple story, but the duel by the cliffs was a classic!

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: Wodetian, how many times did you watch that?!

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Any child in town could recite the plot of Heroes of Yumen. Backwards.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: There's just one detail that this gentleman left out. Qi Qingqiu didn't set his grudge aside when he first saw Shen Feibai in the army.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: It was the Grandmaster who pledged to face Qi Qingqiu's sword on behalf of Shen Feibai, leading to the duel by the cliffs.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Clouds darkened the skies and the winds bellowed, as though heaven and earth were witness to the showdown. The two drew their swords—

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: (In awkward Yanese) Nonsense! Nonsense!

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: Fight look good, but details no, no good!

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: You again, He Xi'an. Do you even know enough Yanese to understand the story?

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: Of course! Heroes of Yumen tell true story fifty year ago. Many hero join together, even though disagreement, still fight together against enemy under Grandmaster.

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: I know many scenes shoot in these inn!

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: 'Were shot', 'this inn'.

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: Looks like you know a thing or two about Yanese history.

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: Of course. Grandmaster tell me when teach me fighting, in Sargon.

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: Grandmaster has sword, but sword special, cannot pull out.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: This again. How could you lose to that Feline girl so easily if you're really the Grandmaster's pupil?

steps.name: Tourist in Sargon Garb
steps.text: What about Feline girl? She very strong. Why you look down her?

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: He's not looking down on her. He's looking down on...

steps.name: Crowd
steps.text: Hahaha...

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: So if the TV show was adapted from a true story, was there really a time in Yumen when kung fu adventurers joined forces with the army against a common foe?

steps.name: Lungmen Tourist
steps.text: To enjoy the freedom of being one's own master, but also achieve great things fighting for one's country... it's pretty cool.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: Well, it's a TV show. The only people who know how things really went down historically are the ones who were there.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: Anyway, swords and spears are out of fashion. If you really want to do something for your country, you should learn Arts and become a Tianshi.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: How would a fortress like Yumen operate, without civilians working to supply its resources?

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: The people who came here to this cold and remote place when the city was first built, and the people who still stay here—they're fighting for their country, in their own way.

steps.name: Drinking Old Man
steps.text: The only thing in the TV show that we know is real for sure, the Grandmaster, is leaving too.
Out of the way.

steps.name: Burly Man
steps.text: The medicine you ordered.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Thanks. Just put it over there; I'll have someone take it to the back.

steps.name: Burly Man
steps.text: I've got the creams for bruising and burns, but we didn't have enough supplies to make herbal meals.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Here's the money. Send my regards to the doc. Oh, and we just had our supplies delivered. Take some back to the clinic.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: There's a lot of stuff. One second, I'll get someone to help.

steps.name: Burly Man
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: He carried the whole cart on his shoulders?!

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: How did the clinic find someone so strong?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Good morning, sir.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I've been here a few days, but I've never seen this place empty.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: We just linked up to resupply with Lungmen a few days ago, only to run into a Catastrophe that forced an emergency separation.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Lots of merchants and tourists were stranded in Yumen, filling up the inns.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Business is good, but it also means more trouble, especially when people who are already frustrated start arguing.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: There are many who would love to have your problem.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Although come to think of it, my head would probably start to hurt if my little business back in Lungmen started getting so busy.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Would you care to start the day with some tea?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Sure. What about the thing I asked you to look into?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Here, the Yumen Arena Board of Fame records from the past six months. Not much I can do if the martial artist you're looking for isn't on it.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: So Yumen operates an arena to this day... such a martial tradition is impressive.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: The Lord Exorcist trains his troops well, and there's no need for folks like us to fight on the battlefield these days. Still, the martial artists need somewhere to hone their kung fu, hence the arena.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Anyway, I would suggest you stay a few days, if it's not urgent. With so many people passing through, someone may have seen the one you're looking for.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: You could also ask at the South Side Sword Forge.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: The shifu there knows the city inside and out. Plus, lots of kung fu fighters hanging around.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Thank you... it's always tough when you don't know the lay of the land.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Mind if I ask what this is about? Are you looking for a friend? An enemy? A debt to repay? Or a debt to collect?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I guess you could say this particular individual owes me a pretty big debt...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: How long will you be this time?

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: No idea.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Will you ever come back?

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: When it's all done.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Do you know that Waai Fu's birthday is in three days?

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: I wasn't a good husband, and I can't be a good father.

steps.name: Huai Tianpei
steps.text: It's enough that I achieve one thing in life.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: A debt to collect, eh? That's gonna be tough. Yan is a big country, and more than a hundred thousand souls live in Yumen alone. Not easy to find someone who doesn't want to be found.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Anyway, your tea's ready. Would you like a side of Yumen-style sauteed meat to go with it?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Sure, I'll take a seat and wait for my girl to finish her match.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Lungmen Spring Tea. Just came in. We only get fresh leaves like these once every few years.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Appreciate it. Feels like a waste to use them on me.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Don't say that. We always value our guests.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm... Spring Tea from Lungmen shouldn't have a bitter taste this time of the year...

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: ...It's you?

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: We weren't supposed to meet here.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Er... excuse me?

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: No... you're not...

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Do you two know each other? Would you care to share a table, since we're pretty full today?

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: No, we don't. I'm not staying long, just a cup of tea.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It's fine, it's fine.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Very well, then. Let me know if you need anything.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Did you mistake me for someone else?

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: You just looked familiar.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Must have been an old friend that you haven't seen for ages.

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: I suppose... stick to your tea.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Have one on me.

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: You're buying me a cup of tea, even though we don't know each other?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: All meetings are the work of fate, even the ones that start with a misunderstanding.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Here's to finding old friends soon.

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: It'll happen when it happens. No point trying to force it.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: That's an interesting answer. The answer lies not in the ones we're looking for, but in the journey of looking for them.

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: Do you talk so much to everyone?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ah, I apologize...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Are you leaving?

steps.name: Aloof Woman
steps.text: I said I wasn't going to stay long.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: How strange...

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Are you sure you don't want to speak to the general first? It's been a while since the last time you came back.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Father is a busy man. I should not bother him at work.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Perhaps I'm being too much of a busybody, but the Department of Discipline and Supervision found your actions faultless in the Shangshu matter. You should not feel guilty about facing the general.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I don't.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: There's nothing for me to do at home anyway. I thought I might as well take a look around town. The Grand Tutor must have sent me to Yumen expecting something to happen. I should keep my eyes open.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I'll come with you, if it's official business.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: It's been years since the last time you were here, hasn't it, Uncle Taihe? It must bring back memories.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Things have changed a lot.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: It's impressive that the general has been able to keep the people of Yumen safe and thriving, with constant warfare going on in the north.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The arena remains as popular as ever.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You still rank fifth on the Board of Fame.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Fame is fleeting. I would be glad to see some young talent knock me off the board.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: The girls in the ring right now...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Did something catch your attention?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I was just thinking how your kung fu would compare to theirs.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Ahem...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Grand Tutor says that a Candleholder's duty is to carry the fire that drives out the shadows of the Feranmut, and to travel amongst to people to learn their troubles.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: A sense of duty comes first, shrewdness second. Kung fu comes third or fourth at best.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: So... How do I compare, then?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: To be frank, while few are as swift as you, in a head-to-head fight, I would say your chances are thirty-seventy, in the other side's favor.
The pair have already traded a dozen moves.
There is hardly time to catch one's breath.
The Feline girl advances, launching a flurry of fists that keeps her opponent's weapon hand in check.
She kicks out. Her opponent, a girl in exotic garb, goes along with it, leaping back with the kick.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Hold!

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: You're out of the ring.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: It's true that you couldn't make full use of your ranged weapons in the ring.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: But rules are rules. It's my win.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: You're very good. And I've never seen anything like your style of fighting.

steps.name: Exotically Dressed Girl
steps.text: (In awkward Yanese) Lose this, no more fights?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: A martial artist shouldn't be too obsessed with victory and defeat, but I can't lose here.

steps.name: Exotically Dressed Girl
steps.text: You want the sword too?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Sword? What sword?

steps.name: Exotically Dressed Girl
steps.text: People in the city say, number one on the Board of Fame can get the special sword.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: No... I just wanted to climb the rankings so my name can be seen.

steps.name: Exotically Dressed Girl
steps.text: You number 31. Means 30 people stronger than you?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: ...I suppose so.

steps.name: Exotically Dressed Girl
steps.text: You are better than me.

steps.name: Exotically Dressed Girl
steps.text: (I guess this won't work...)

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Hey, where are you going?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: If I win this, I make it to the first page of the Board of Fame.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: But will he see it?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Round 15. The Millenion was hit in the right wrist, right pectoral, central abdomen and throat. Qiubai was not hit. Qiubai is the winner.

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: Haha, I would have died three times, if this were a real battle.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: Real battles are about the mind as much as kung fu. Who knows how things would have turned out?

steps.name: Millenion
steps.text: You are indeed the Grandmaster's student. It was humbling.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: I would like to see the Grandmaster's comments.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The recent ones are all here. The Grandmaster has been paying close attention to your bouts, despite his busy schedule, and he has high praise in particular for your swordsmanship.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Something on your mind?

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: I was just thinking what he meant by 'not enough purity in the sword.'

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: And how long would it take for me to reach the point where I can beat him.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: There is no mention of it in the Grandmaster's Book of Kung Fu. I don't think he said it to anyone but you.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: As for beating the Grandmaster... I'm not sure how many in the entire world have even dreamt of such a thing.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: You think I'm crazy?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: My job is simply to follow the Grandmaster and record the martial arts of the world truthfully.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: There are many more people than usual at the training grounds today. Why isn't he here?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: General Zuo has visitors. The Grandmaster is also meeting an old acquaintance in the keep.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: I'll be going, then.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Man zou. It was an honor.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: Why do you always treat me like I'm your senior, even though you've been following the Grandmaster for much longer?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The Grandmaster says that one who keeps records must be acutely aware of the strengths of others.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: You are stronger and wiser than I am. I have much to learn from you.

steps.name: Qiubai
steps.text: If you say so.
The general nocks an arrow, drawing the thick bow so full that it looks like the full moon.
The hand on the bow trembles slightly, and the arrow wobbles with it. The general's brow furrows deeper with each wobble.
The arrow pierces the target, half an inch away from the bullseye.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Good shot, sir.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: No need to flatter. I know my own body.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I could still swing the sword and spear a couple of years ago, but now I can hardly hold a bow properly.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Even if there's no need for me to stand on the battlefield myself, it's not proper to have a sick man leading the Yumen garrison... my time is short.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: All the court knows that your injuries bear witness to decades of service in defense of Yumen.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I'm not concerned about my health or life, but I have some unfinished business.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The Grand Tutor has instructed me to assist you. I will help you manage Yumen's return.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Did the Grand Tutor say 'assist?'

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I'm sure you understand his intentions...

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I haven't thanked you for your help in Shangshu yet. I apologize for the trouble that Zuo Le caused. He's still young and inexperienced.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You exaggerate, sir.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You must understand what a father feels.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Zuo Le has done well, but he is in a position that does not permit any mistake, no matter how small.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Lord Zuo is young and bright, a rising star. It's not unusual for young people to be a little impetuous. I would not worry too much about it.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: What about me, Liang? Am I impetuous to you?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...I believe you have your reasons, sir.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Word of your benevolent administration in Shangshu has reached even Yumen, Liang, but have you ever seen a battle with your own eyes?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: There were pirates on the Shangshu River a few years ago... but nothing compared to the battles that you have seen.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Then you understand that making decisions as a general in the field is different from managing at a desk.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: The battlefield is ever-changing, and thousands of lives hinge on your every decision.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Which do you think is more important then: decisiveness, or caution?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: The bestial Sui matter is pressing. We must act.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I am much illuminated.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: In your position as Yumen Advisor, you are on the battlefield, and we are comrades. I hope you understand my way.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I trust you, sir. I'll give my all.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: However, the Feranmut problem is neither administrative nor military.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I trust your decisiveness, but I also ask that you trust my caution.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Right...
Another arrow, this one striking the bullseye square.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Would you care to try, Liang?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Your reputation is that of a scholar-warrior, equally at home with sword and bow as with pen and paper.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: The Yumen bow is heavy, though. Do you feel up to it?

steps.name: Patrol Battalion Soldier
steps.text: Chief Executive Wei Yenwu of Lungmen is here, sir. He's waiting in the meeting hall.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Mr. Lin's daughter was a few days early. It was about time for Lord Wei to arrive.

steps.name: Patrol Battalion Soldier
steps.text: The Grand Tutor has arrived as well.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Did the Grand Tutor and Lord Wei travel together?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I expect Lord Wei is here on private matters.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Official or private, there are still two honored guests at the same table.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Looks like you're not the only one here to give me counsel today, Liang.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: My dear elder brother.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I had a dream last night.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I dreamed I heard the wind rushing by at midnight. I opened the window to find the desert had become a sea of sprouting trees, some of them even in full bloom.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: The branches of the trees grew and formed a web, trapping Yumen within.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: 'Few are those who truly break away from home.'

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Do you still miss Yumen?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: What was the saying you had when you left Yumen last time? I forgot.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: 'Neath crisp night merriment resounds; travelers doubt 'its truly frontier-bound.'

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: A new one. It's been a while; looks like your thoughts have changed.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: A century is not too long, but I came back at this point in the dream.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: To me, a hundred years is simply thirty thousand days and nights, the urgent reports, the scouts departing, the Messengers returning.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: The watch has changed innumerable times since you left, and countless new bricks and stones set into this wall.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: But still it stands.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Did you see Nian and Dusk in Shangshu?

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Yea. They haven't changed one bit. They've found a place to stay, a place where they can have fun.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: And so, you met our second brother.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: We lesser siblings always worry our eldest brother, don't we?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Dusk is a sensitive and thoughtful little sister, but she keeps it to herself and tells no one, which is why she's often troubled.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Nian looks carefree on the surface, but she fears loneliness more than any of us. She constantly needs something new to keep her mind occupied.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I don't have much to worry about you, other than maybe you getting too drunk and forgetting to pay your tab.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: But as the oldest sister, and without any official responsibilities, it would be good if you spent more time with your younger siblings.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Do you accuse me of being an irresponsible big sister?

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: How many families are like ours? From whom do I learn? I have to figure things out on my own.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: But our foolish sisters just don't know how to rise above things. They keep making it hard for themselves.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Don't blame them for being self-troubled. Put yourself in their shoes, and you may not find it easy to free yourself from troubles.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: I'm not as free as you are. After all, you've managed to completely cut your 'Self' off, and find an entirely new 'Self'.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: The name 'Shuo' and the sliver of soul are sealed within the sword. Now I'm just an ordinary man who knows a little kung fu.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: 'A little?' How many martial artists would abandon their careers if they heard you just now?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Taking into account the fact that I've had centuries of practice, perhaps I should call myself less than ordinary.
The sand sluice there churns through tons of sand every second, clearing a path for Yumen's advance.
The massive nomadic city rolls toward its new goal at high speed.

steps.name: Ling
steps.text: Where are you planning to go after you leave Yumen?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I'll go south to see the bridges and streams, have some of the heartland brew, or see the place where Nian and Dusk are staying.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: The jianghu world is big. There are plenty of places to go.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: But I suppose all the people with whom I've shared a toast are gone now.
In the distance, the heat rising from the ocean of sands warps heaven and earth.
The wind is weak by the time it reaches the tower. The sand in the wind touches the cheeks, almost like a caress.
Three thousand miles of yellow sand, in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Yumen Sentry A
steps.text: Checked the serial numbers on the gear. It's the Catastrophe Messenger's group, which should have been back this morning.

steps.name: Yumen Sentry A
steps.text: Traces of Originium explosives. The bodies have probably crystalized and turned to dust...

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Watch out for Originium residue.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: This is less than two hours from the city. Who would attack a Catastrophe Messenger on official business so close to a nomadic city?

steps.name: Yumen Sentry A
steps.text: Everything valuable has been taken. It would make sense if this was the work of bandits.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Or someone who wants to make it look like the work of bandits.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Keep looking. We need to find the Catastrophe survey data.

steps.name: Yumen Sentry B
steps.text: Found it!

steps.name: Yumen Sentry B
steps.text: It was a little further away, under a piece of broken armor.

steps.name: Yumen Sentry B
steps.text: They protected it with their lives.
